questions.q: According to Hollis, how are boys and girls typically raised differently?
a: Boys are raised to chase dreams, girls to meet expectations
Boys are praised for effort, girls for good grades
Boys learn to share, girls learn to compete
Boys are taught patience, girls are taught ambition
questions.why: Lesson 1 says boys are brought up to follow their dreams while girls follow what is expected.

questions.q: What does Hollis say you must do instead of waiting for free time?
a: Make time for your goals by sacrificing something
Wake up earlier every single morning
Cut your goal down to a smaller size
Ask your family for uninterrupted hours
questions.why: Lesson 2 tells readers to stop looking for free time and start making time for their goals.

questions.q: What is the first step in Hollis's 10-10-1 goal plan?
a: Picture your life ten years from now in detail
List ten habits you want to build this year
Choose one goal you can finish in ten weeks
Ask ten friends to review your goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 starts the plan by imagining your life a decade ahead and writing down specifics.

questions.q: How does Hollis suggest wording a goal?
a: As a measurable target written in the present tense
As a question you answer each morning
As a list of daily habits to track
As a promise to a friend or mentor
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to write the goal as if achieved and make it measurable, like a bank balance.

questions.q: What does Hollis say about people who judge you?
a: They will judge you whatever you do, so ignore them
They usually change their minds once you succeed
They are the best source of honest feedback
They should be cut out of your life entirely
questions.why: Lesson 2 says judgmental people will find reasons to judge you no matter what you do.
